fixes.explanation: Baked just right on the geography, baker! The text says Israel traveled "…from place to place until the cloud settled in the Wilderness of Paran." (Numbers 10:12) So the cloud settles in Paran. Israel's trip is a whole string of places before that.

Zin is a good guess, friend, but it's not the one in this verse. Numbers 10:12 says the cloud settled "…in the Wilderness of Paran." Israel traveled from place to place before the cloud settled there. I'd have guessed wrong too, and I can't even work a map.

Shur is a fine guess, but the verse names a different spot. Numbers 10:12 says the cloud settled "…in the Wilderness of Paran." Israel traveled from place to place first. Paran is where the cloud settles at the end of that stretch.

Not quite, friend. The text says Israel set out "…according to the LORD’s command through Moses." (Numbers 10:13) That's the reason it gives for this first time they set out. The command came from the LORD, and Moses is the one it came through.

An army? Friend, that's a whole different invitation. Moses never brings one up. He says, "…for the LORD has promised good things to Israel." (Numbers 10:29) His pitch is a promise, plus "we will treat you well." Not a word about troops.

Kings and diplomacy? Nope, Moses isn't asking Hobab to be a talker. He says, "…you know where we should camp in the wilderness, and you can serve as our eyes." (Numbers 10:31) The skill on the table is knowing where to camp. Hobab is wanted for his eyes, not his small talk.

That's right, baker! The text says "…the ark of the covenant of the LORD…" was "…traveling ahead of them for those three days…" (Numbers 10:33) The ark goes out in front, and Israel sets out from the mountain of the LORD behind it. Three days of that.

Moses is in this story, but he's not who the verse puts out in front. It says "…the ark of the covenant of the LORD…" was "…traveling ahead of them for those three days…" (Numbers 10:33) No staff gets mentioned in this passage. The ark is the one named as going ahead.

The golden lampstand is a lovely piece, but it doesn't show up in this passage. What does show up is "…the ark of the covenant of the LORD…" "…traveling ahead of them for those three days…" (Numbers 10:33) I'd love a lampstand out front too, but the text names the ark. Next time, go with the ark.

A meeting place sounds sensible, friend, but that's not the word in the verse. The ark goes ahead "…to seek a resting place for them." (Numbers 10:33) The word is resting. Think of a long trip and ask yourself what you'd want at the end of it.

Hiding is a creative pick, but it's not the word here. The verse says the ark goes ahead "…to seek a resting place for them." (Numbers 10:33) Resting is what the ark is looking for. After three days on the road, I'd be looking for the same thing, and probably a chair.

Water would be a fine thing to ask for, friend. Moses doesn't ask for it here, though. He says, "Rise up, O LORD! May Your enemies be scattered; may those who hate You flee before You." (Numbers 10:35) His words are about the LORD's enemies being scattered. That's what he calls out whenever the ark sets out.
